confirmed.title: Sheet outbox stalls: entries the script skips are never deleted, and the script only ever lists the first 12 entries by id
confirmed.scenario:
1. An admin adds a new intake resident (rid 202701) in People, so residents/202701 exists. isMember() passes and the rules accept their sheetOutbox entries (validOutbox only checks that rid is a string of at most 40 characters that matches the logbook's rid).
2. The response sheet's Residents tab doesn't have 202701 yet. That is normal for a few days at intake, and OUTBOX-README.md says such entries 'wait in the outbox'.
3. The resident logs 20 to 30 cases. Each run, logbookOutboxAdd_ skips those entries ('no resident 202701 on the Residents sheet', line 136) and does not delete them, because only r.done is removed (line 170).
4. logbookOutboxList_ (line 233) fetches '?pageSize=12' with no orderBy and no page token. Firestore's REST list returns documents in __name__ (id) order, so every run gets the same first 12 ids. Once 12 or more skipped entries have the lowest ids, every other resident's entry with a higher id is never listed.
5. The same happens forever for any rid that isn't 6 digits (line 135). The admin tools don't enforce 6 digits.
confirmed.consequence: Without warning, the response sheet (Case tab, Database, AY totals) stops getting most new app cases from all programme residents, so the sheet's counts fall behind the app's. The run reports 'added 0, skipped 12' with console.warn only. Skips are not errors, so logbookOutboxRun never throws and Google never sends a failure email. The nightly Totals check compares the sheet with itself, so it can't catch this. When the resident is finally added to the Residents tab, the backlog drains slowly; a rid that isn't 6 digits never clears.
confirmed.fix: List a larger page (e.g. pageSize=300, or follow nextPageToken up to a cap) and process at most LOGBOOK_OUTBOX_BATCH entries that aren't skipped. Count skipped entries older than about a day as errors, so the run throws and the owner gets the failure email. Optionally have validOutbox require rid.matches('^[0-9]{6}$') so an entry the script can never place is refused at the source.

confirmed.title: A resident added to the programme list after first using the app has one session whose new cases never reach the response sheet (and photo saves are refused)
confirmed.scenario:
1. A resident signs in on their phone before an admin adds them to residents/. app.js caches the 'who' answer with resident: null (saveWho, localStorage).
2. The admin adds them to the list. Next time the resident opens the app (or reloads a PWA left open), onUser takes the fast path: known = the cached who, so S.resident is null at start and the rid save at app.js:1016 (`if (resident && logbook.rid !== resident.rid) cloud.saveLogbook(...{ rid })`) does not run.
3. refreshWho (app.js:930-951) then finds the resident and sets S.resident, but it never saves the rid. logbooks/{email}.rid stays null on the server, and S.logbook.rid stays null on the device.
4. The resident logs cases for the rest of the session, which can be days for an installed app. toSheet (ui-core.js:454) requires `S.logbook?.rid === S.resident.rid`, so it queues nothing. Even if it did, the rules' isMember() (firestore.rules:272-277, needed for the sheetOutbox create) checks logbooks/{me}.rid, so the server would refuse the entry.
5. The next session saves the rid. Nothing ever re-queues the earlier cases: the outbox is written only at creation.
Second trigger: onUser saves the rid with cloud.saveLogbook but never sets S.logbook.rid. If any patchLogbook replaces S.logbook before refreshWho's server reload, then refreshWho's `S.logbook === firstLogbook` check fails and the device keeps rid null for that session.
confirmed.consequence: Cases logged in that session are in the app but never reach the response sheet, so the app's counts are permanently higher than the sheet's for that resident. Also in that session: '+ Add image' is shown because S.resident is set, but saveImage is refused by isMember() ('Could not add image: Missing or insufficient permissions'). A Word portfolio import drops every figure silently: ui-reflect-import.js only logs 'figure skipped' and moves the caption into the summary. A backup restore with photos stops with 'Restore stopped' before its reflections, because images are restored first.
confirmed.fix: Write the rid wherever the resident becomes known. In refreshWho, after S.resident is set and the server logbook is adopted: `if (S.resident && S.logbook && S.logbook.rid !== S.resident.rid) patchLogbook({ rid: S.resident.rid })`. In onUser, use the same local and cloud update so S.logbook.rid is set at once. Firestore sends writes in order, so a later sheetOutbox create sees the rid. Optionally, when the rid is first saved, queue outbox entries for that session's own source app/paste cases.
verifier_fix:
The proposed fix is basically right, with these details:
1. In refreshWho, put the rid write before the early `return` (`if (!lbChanged && before === ...) return;`). Otherwise a session where nothing else changed still skips it. Use `if (S.resident?.rid && S.logbook && S.logbook.rid !== S.resident.rid) patchLogbook({ rid: S.resident.rid });`, after the server logbook is adopted. patchLogbook is already used in app.js through adoptShared.
2. In onUser, replace the bare `cloud.saveLogbook(...)` with `patchLogbook({ rid: resident.rid })`, or set `S.logbook.rid` locally as well. Then the device has the rid at once, whether or not refreshWho later adopts the server copy.
3. Firestore sends one client's writes in order, so a sheetOutbox or image create queued after that patch sees the rid.
4. Optional back-fill when the rid is first written: queue that session's app/paste cases. This is safe to repeat: the sheetOutbox rules allow create only (a duplicate is refused), and Outbox.gs skips any `app:<caseId>` already in column J.
5. Add a regression test for the late-added path. A demo-mode script like the repro is enough: off the list, then added, then check that `S.logbook.rid` is set and the toSheet gate opens in the same session.
6. A rules-side alternative for the outbox only: validate sheetOutbox with `isResident(request.resource.data.rid)` (residents/{rid}.email == me) instead of the logbook rid, and drop the `S.logbook.rid` check from toSheet. Images still need the logbook rid, so the client fix is still needed.

confirmed.title: 'Plan for later' silently drops the oldest planned cases to fit the rules' 100-item cap, and Undo can write a plan the rules refuse
confirmed.scenario:
1. validLogbook allows `plan.size() <= 100` (firestore.rules:153).
2. A resident pastes their next-day lists with 'Plan for later' and ticks them off in batches, so overdue items (cases already done but not yet confirmed) build up to, say, 90.
3. They paste a 15-line list and choose Tomorrow. put() saves `[...plan(), ...items].slice(-100)`, which drops the 5 oldest planned cases, and the toast still says 'Planned 15 cases'.
4. Separately, the Undo on '✓ All N done' (line 1169) does deleteMany(...) and then `savePlan([...plan(), ...items])` with no cap. If the plan has grown since, the write goes over 100, the rules refuse it, and only a 'Could not save settings' toast appears. The logged cases are already deleted, and the items stay only in the local S.logbook until a reload.
confirmed.consequence: Cases the resident actually did, and was waiting to confirm, vanish from the plan without notice and are never logged, so the counts come out lower. In the Undo path the cases are gone from both the logbook and the plan.
confirmed.fix: In put(), if plan().length + items.length > 100, plan nothing and say how many fit, or ask the resident to confirm or remove overdue items first. Never slice off existing items. In the Undo, check the cap before deleteMany and save the plan first, deleting the cases only if the plan save succeeded.
verifier_fix: Fix only put(). Drop the .slice(-100). If plan().length + items.length > 100, save nothing and leave the pasted rows on screen. Say how many fit, for example: 'Your plan already holds N cases (100 at most). Confirm or remove the overdue ones first, or Save all now.' Also refuse a single paste of more than 100 rows the same way. The Undo needs no change: the plan cannot grow between Done and Undo on one device (no live listener on the logbook doc, and one toast at a time). Reordering it to 'save plan first, delete only on success' would not work anyway: patchLogbook swallows errors, and queued() resolves after 3 s offline. At most, add a defensive cap check.

confirmed.title: Deleting a case offline shows 'A change could not be synced: Missing or insufficient permissions' because the sheetOutbox delete of an entry that no longer exists is always refused
confirmed.scenario:
1. A programme resident deletes a case (bin, multi-select, or Undo) that was logged more than about 5 minutes ago, or that came from the Form or the import. Its sheetOutbox entry no longer exists or never did.
2. removeCase / deleteMany call offSheet (ui-core.js:458), which calls cloud.dropSheetRows. That wraps F.deleteDoc in queued() (cloud.js:678-681).
3. The rule `allow delete: if isFormBot() || (signedIn() && resource.data.email == me())`: for a document that doesn't exist, resource is null, so resource.data is an error and the delete is denied. The code's own comment on the same-shaped formInbox rule (cloud.js:654: 'an entry already picked up on another device (its delete refused)') shows this behaviour is known.
4. Online, the refusal comes back within ACK_WAIT and Promise.allSettled swallows it. Offline (theatre) or on a link slower than 3 s, it arrives late, so queued() passes it to onSyncError, and app.js:1163 shows the toast once per deleted case when signal returns.
confirmed.consequence: No data is lost: the case delete itself synced. But the resident is told a change failed to sync, which in this app means 'your data may not be saved'. They may redo deletions, distrust the sync status, or report false data loss. The false alarm also buries real late-sync errors.
confirmed.fix: Rules: `allow delete: if isFormBot() || (signedIn() && (resource == null || resource.data.email == me()));`. Deleting nothing is harmless. Add a rules test for a resident deleting a missing outbox entry. Or on the client, don't route dropSheetRows through queued()'s late-error reporting: race `F.deleteDoc(...).catch(() => {})` with a timeout.
